analysis.one_liner: Muthoot Finance is India's largest gold-loan NBFC, lending against pledged household gold jewellery, with microfinance, housing and vehicle-loan units alongside the core gold business.
analysis.whats_happening: Q2 FY27 results are due around 5 Nov 2026 (board meeting date not yet fixed), roughly two and a half weeks out. The stock is sitting at a 52-week low of ₹2,559.6, and a new Managing Director, Alexander George, took charge on 1 Oct 2026 as part of a long-planned family succession - George Alexander Muthoot moved to Executive Vice Chairman and K.R. Bijimon was elevated to CEO. In the last reported quarter (Q1 FY27, June 2026), consolidated profit rose 43% year-on-year to ₹2,825 crore, but margins compressed sharply versus the preceding quarter.
analysis.plain_terms: Profit looks fantastic on a year-on-year basis, up 43%, but the more telling comparison is sequential: the margin Muthoot earns on its loan book fell from 13.38% to 10.41% in one quarter because it is deliberately pricing loans more competitively to grow faster. The stock has fallen 36% from its January 2026 peak - there is no split or demerger behind this move, it is a genuine price decline. The market is betting that the exceptionally rich margins of FY26 were temporary, not that the business itself is broken.
analysis.quarters: Q1 FY27 (June 2026): consolidated PAT ₹2,825 cr (+43% YoY from ₹1,974 cr); standalone PAT ₹2,550 cr (+25% YoY). Consolidated AUM ₹1,91,532 cr (+43% YoY, +5% QoQ); gold-loan AUM ₹1,63,298 cr (+44% YoY). Sequentially, however, consolidated profit fell ~17% from Q4 FY26's ₹3,397.5 cr, and net interest margin dropped 297 bps (13.38% to 10.41%) as yield on loan assets fell from 20.76% to 17.93%. Management's framing: Q4 FY26 was flattered by one-off interest recoveries and loan renewals, while the current quarter reflects a deliberate shift toward more competitive, lower-rate lending to keep volume growth up - a strategic trade-off, not a quality problem. Gross Stage III (NPA) improved to 2.28% from 2.58% a year earlier; capital adequacy stood at 20.3%.
analysis.performance_read: No splits or corporate actions sit behind this chart (has_corporate_action: false), so the 36% drawdown from the January 2026 peak of ₹4,057 to the current ₹2,598 is a real price decline, not a demerger artifact. Over 1 year the stock is down 19.83% against Nifty's -9.53% and peer Manappuram's +13.86% - a clear, recent underperformance against both the index and its closest comparable. Zoom out, though: over 3 years (+114.98%) and 5 years (+79.01%) Muthoot has roughly kept pace with Manappuram (+136.75%/+80.7%) and comfortably beaten the Nifty (+16.83%/+25.27%). The pain is concentrated in the last twelve months, not a multi-year pattern.
analysis.valuation_read: Trading near ₹2,598, Muthoot's P/E is about 9.2x and P/B about 2.6x against a book value of roughly ₹1,011/share, with ROE near 31% and ROCE near 15.8%. Why it looks cheap: the market is pricing in margin normalisation after the unusually rich FY26 (the 297bps NIM compression just reported) and lingering uncertainty from RBI's gold-loan lending directions (tiered loan-to-value caps of 75-85% depending on loan size) that have been in force since 1 April 2026. Whether it is actually cheap is a separate question - a 9x multiple against a 31% ROE looks statistically inexpensive for an NBFC, but if margins structurally settle lower than FY26's levels, the multiple may simply be correctly pricing a smaller future profit pool rather than offering a bargain.
analysis.growth_read: This is volume-led growth, not margin-led. Consolidated AUM is up 43% YoY and gold-loan AUM up 44% YoY, but yield on loan assets fell from 20.76% to 17.93% and NIM compressed sharply in the same period - management is explicitly trading margin for market share by pricing more competitively. In a collateral-backed lending business this can be durable, but it means each additional rupee lent now earns less than it did a year ago.
analysis.health_read: Cash conversion looks healthy for now: Gross Stage III assets improved to 2.28% (from 2.58% a year ago) and credit losses are near 0.05% of gross loans, while capital adequacy of 20.3% sits well above the regulatory floor. Because Muthoot lends against low-LTV, short-tenure gold collateral, the underlying business (credit) risk has historically been modest; the more relevant risk for an NBFC like this is financial/funding risk - the cost and availability of its wholesale borrowings (bank lines, bonds, commercial paper) - rather than loan losses. Nothing in the current data points to funding stress.
analysis.ownership_read: Promoter family holding is 73.35%, unchanged across every reported quarter from March 2024 through June 2026, with 0% pledged - a clean and stable base. Individual family members (George Thomas, George Jacob Muthoot, Susan Thomas, Sara George) each hold roughly 7-11% directly. FIIs hold 10.84% and DIIs 12.21%. Available data did not surface any marquee outside individual investor on the register - none is noted holding a disclosable stake.
strengths: Gold-loan AUM up 44% YoY to ₹1,63,298 cr and consolidated AUM up 43% YoY to ₹1,91,532 cr (Q1 FY27)
Asset quality improving: Gross Stage III (NPA) at 2.28% versus 2.58% a year ago, credit losses near 0.05% of gross loans
Capital adequacy of 20.3%, comfortably above the regulatory minimum, with zero promoter pledge on a stable 73.35% holding
Dividend has risen every year from ₹12 (FY19) to ₹30 (FY26), including through the COVID years
watchpoints: Net interest margin compressed 297 bps quarter-on-quarter (13.38% to 10.41%) as yield on loan assets fell from 20.76% to 17.93% - a margin reset, not yet confirmed as a new steady state
Stock down 36% from its January 2026 peak and sitting at a 52-week low; it has underperformed both the Nifty and peer Manappuram over the past year (-19.83% vs -9.53% and +13.86%)
Leadership transition effective 1 Oct 2026 (new MD, new CEO, reshuffled board) - a planned family succession, but still a change worth tracking through a few quarters
RBI's Gold Loan Directions (tiered LTV caps of 75-85% by loan size, in force since 1 April 2026) structurally cap how much can be lent against larger pledges, a persistent headwind on yields
analysis.one_thing: The Q2 FY27 results (expected around 5 Nov 2026) - specifically whether NIM stabilises near the 10-11% reported in Q1 FY27 or keeps falling - will show whether the margin compression was a one-quarter reset or an ongoing trend.
analysis.data_notes: Q1 FY27 (June 2026 quarter) PAT and AUM figures were cross-checked across multiple independent sources (Free Press Journal, GuruFocus earnings-call summary, Business Upturn) and agree directionally. P/E (~9.2x), ROE (~30.9%), ROCE (~15.8%) and book value came from an aggregator (screener-style site) consistent with the supplied closing price. Shareholding (73.35% promoter, 0% pledge) was consistent across two independent trackers for the June 2026 quarter. The Q4 FY26 PAT (₹3,397.5 cr) and the 13.38%→10.41% NIM figures came from a single explanatory article and were not independently cross-verified against the company's own press release - treat these two figures as reported but not primary-source confirmed.
